description: Ribollita is a hearty Tuscan peasant soup, traditionally "reboiled" the day after it's made, giving it an incredible depth of flavor and a thick, satisfying texture. This robust vegetable and bread soup is a true comfort food, perfect for cooler evenings, showcasing simple ingredients transformed into something extraordinary. Its name, meaning "reboiled," highlights the traditional method of reheating it, which further enhances its rich, rustic character.

instructions.title: Prepare the Soffritto
instructions.text: In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat the extra virgin olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion, carrots, and celery. Sauté gently until the vegetables have softened and become translucent, which typically takes about 8 to 10 minutes.

instructions.title: Add Aromatics and Greens
instructions.text: Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another minute until it becomes fragrant. Be careful not to let the garlic brown. Add the chopped black cabbage (cavolo nero) and Swiss chard to the pot, stirring frequently until the greens wilt down significantly, about 5 to 7 minutes.

instructions.title: Build the Soup Base
instructions.text: Pour in the crushed tomatoes and approximately half of the vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Add the cooked cannellini beans, reserving a small handful (about 50g) to mash later for thickening. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to your liking.

instructions.title: Simmer and Thicken
instructions.text: Continue to simmer the soup uncovered for about 20 minutes, allowing all the flavors to meld beautifully. Meanwhile, mash the reserved cannellini beans with a fork or potato masher until creamy, then stir them back into the soup. This will help to naturally thicken the Ribollita.

instructions.title: Layer with Bread
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). In an oven-safe casserole dish, arrange a layer of the stale Tuscan bread slices at the bottom. Ladle about a third of the hot soup over the bread, ensuring it is well soaked. Repeat this layering process two more times, ending with a generous top layer of soup.

instructions.title: The "Reboil" and Serve
instructions.text: Cover the casserole dish and bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until the bread has fully absorbed the liquid and the soup is bubbling hot. For an even more traditional experience, let the soup cool completely and then reheat it the next day on the stovetop or in the oven; this "reboiling" is key to its name. Serve hot, drizzled generously with fresh extra virgin olive oil and optionally sprinkled with grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

tips: For authentic flavor, use true Tuscan stale bread which is unsalted. If using regular country bread, adjust salt in the soup accordingly.

The 'twice boiled' aspect is crucial. Making the soup a day ahead and reheating it slowly on the stovetop or in the oven allows the flavors to deepen and the bread to fully integrate, giving it that characteristic thick texture.
Always finish your Ribollita with a generous drizzle of high-quality extra virgin olive oil just before serving. It adds a wonderful peppery note and richness that is essential to the dish.
